sources.title: CJCR Gp Dress Instructions, Chapter 3 Annex D
sources.status: Figure notes 3D-3, 3D-5 and 3D-6 supplied verbatim by Lt Beal, 2026-09-24.
sources.note_3D-3_verbatim: Worn on the right sleeve of the cadet jacket in their order of precedence, 1 cm above the Star Level badge. Advanced qualification supersedes basic qualification.
sources.note_3D-5_verbatim: These badges shall be worn with the participation badges on the right sleeve in the order that they are awarded. The first badge awarded is centred immediately above the cuff of the uniform jacket. The second badge awarded is placed immediately to the left of the first badge, to the front of the sleeve. The third badge awarded is placed immediately to the right of the first badge, to the rear of the sleeve. The fourth, fifth and sixth badges are placed immediately above badges one, two and three forming a second row of badges and they are placed in the same order as the first row. If a seventh badge is awarded, it shall be placed immediately over the fourth badge. Only a maximum of seven badges shall be worn.
sources.note_3D-6_verbatim: The Glider Pilot CTC badge is never worn with the Glider Pilot Wings. Issued Glider Pilot / Power Pilot sewn (nylon thread) insignia shall be worn centred directly above the left breast pocket and horizontal on the cadet jacket and flight suit. Glider Pilot / Power Pilot pin may be purchased and worn on the collared shirt when the jacket is removed, directly centred 0.5 cm over the left breast pocket. Silver and Gold wire thread embroidered Glider Pilot / Power Pilot badges may be purchased by the cadet and are authorized for wear only on the uniform jacket in lieu of issued wings. If a cadet successfully completes both Scholarships, only the Power Pilot Wings shall be worn. The Glider Pilot Scholarship CTC Qualification Badge shall then be worn with the other CTC Qualification Badges.
sources.dating: Lt Beal: the section text (CH3S1 for Army, para 3 for Sea and Air) is dated newer than these figure notes, so where the two disagree the section text governs.

sources.title: CJCR Gp O 10050 - JCR National Honours and Awards
sources.status: SECONDARY. This order governs the Junior Canadian Ranger programme, not the Cadet programme, and states placement for the JCR sweatshirt rather than the cadet tunic. It is used here for ORDER, not for GEOMETRY: para 4.2 records that the CJCR Honours and Awards committee 'includes both JCR and Cadet Program personnel' and 'determines eligibility criteria and order of precedence', and the medal list at 7.4 spans all three cadet elements including the Sea, Army and Air Cadet Service Medals - so the precedence itself is CJCR-wide, not JCR-specific. Every cadet-facing geometric figure still comes from Chapter 5. Para 4.4 points at Chapter 7 of the Cadet and JCR Dress Instructions; Lt Beal confirms Chapter 7 is the JCR-specific chapter, so it does not supersede the Chapter 5 citations used throughout this pack.

datums.shoulder_seam: Upper seam of the sleeve at the shoulder. Offsets measured downward.
datums.cuff_bottom: Bottom edge of the cuff, not the top cuff seam. Offsets measured upward.
datums.pocket_top: Top edge of the breast pocket. Front offsets measured upward. One frame per pocket, left and right.
datums.pocket_flap_bottom: Lower edge of the breast pocket flap. Pocket-mounted pins are centred between this and the pocket's lower seam.

measured_constants_cm.$comment: All values in cm. Policy gives only gaps between items, never badge sizes, so these are local measurements. 'confidence' flags how much weight a renderer should put on each.

star_level_badge.note: Inner/outer ratio is 0.667. A classic pentagram star is 0.382, so this is a noticeably fatter star. Renderer must build from the two diameters, not from a default star primitive.

marksmanship_rifles.note: Both dimensions measured by Lt Beal. Supersedes w=5.5, which was inferred from the poster aspect 0.742 and is 8% low. Same width as the Distinguished assembly. Poster artwork trims to aspect 1.003 (square), implying 5.98 cm tall at this width against the 5.08 cm measured - treat poster aspects as unreliable for sizing.

marksmanship_crowned.note: Distinguished only. Single piece, replaces rifles + numeral. Remeasured by Lt Beal and confirmed. Poster artwork trims to aspect 0.831 against the 0.750 measured; the measurement stands.

rank_chevron.note: Cdt wears no rank insignia. Heights step +1.5 cm per rank. RESOLVED against the poster: poster aspects imply LCpl 7.41 / Cpl 8.98 / MCpl 10.13 / Sgt 12.02 cm at 10 cm wide. Lt Beal's hand measurement governs - the poster art carries an embroidered field the finished badge does not, and artwork identifies badges without dimensioning them.

rank_mwo.note: RESOLVED against the poster: the recorded bounding box gives aspect 1.50 against the 1.26 drawn. Lt Beal's hand measurement governs, on the same grounds as the chevrons.

rank_cwo.note: Guess only. Suspect: MWO is landscape (wider than tall) and this estimate is portrait and twice MWO's height. CWO insignia is the coat of arms rather than a crown so a taller box is plausible, but measure before trusting.

appointment_badge.confidence: measured for pipe major and drum major only
appointment_badge.note: Same 10 x 11 cm bounding box as Sgt rank. Anchored by its bottom edge at 20 cm, so it spans 20 to 31 cm above the cuff bottom. Other appointment insignia not measured.

circle_badge.note: 3 cm confirmed geometrically. The CTC grid is 3 circles wide. At 3 cm the grid is 9 cm on a 12.26 cm flat sleeve at that height, leaving 1.63 cm each side. At 4 cm it would be 12 cm on the same 12.26 cm, leaving 0.13 cm each side, which cannot be sewn. Measured on size 6436; smaller sizes make the 4 cm case worse still.
circle_badge.level_identifier: None. Music levels are now built into the circle rather than carried on a separate numeral.

expedition_pin.note: Circular. Poster draws it at roughly 1.5x the championship pins in the same block, which is a within-band comparison and so more trustworthy than a cross-band one - 1 in is probably low. Still an estimate; measure one.

competition_pin.note: Applies to the CHAMPIONSHIP pins only (zone, provincial, national) in both the marksmanship and biathlon streams. Poster artwork trims to aspect 1.00-1.03, consistent with a square. Air's Effective Speaking pins take the same size (Lt Beal, 2026-09-24).

corps_name_title.note: Derived, not measured. The poster draws the corps name title and the RCAC badge together as one template, twice, for two example corps (manifest items 15 and 17; both pixel-identical). Title is 1.923 x the badge diameter wide and 0.606 x it tall, so the measured 6.35 cm diameter fixes both. Leaves 1.8 cm of cloth between the title's bottom edge and the badge's top. The renderer now draws 242 Fredericton's own title, generated by art/Shoulder Title Kit/make_corps_title.py onto the issued blank plate. It reuses the same 1721 x 542 canvas as the poster artwork, so the 3.175 aspect and therefore the derived dimensions are unchanged - only the lettering differs.

rcac_badge.note: Measured locally by Lt Beal. Artwork on the poster is a true circle (895 x 895 px trimmed), which agrees.

breast_pocket.note: 13 cm across the top edge, 15 cm top to bottom. Taller than wide, which is unusual for a patch pocket, so it was previously flagged as possibly transposed - Lt Beal has confirmed the orientation explicitly. Load-bearing for every front placement.

competition_pin_strip.note: Fits exactly three 1 in pins with 0.23 cm side clearance and 0.34 cm gaps. Independently confirms the CH3S1 4.b cap of three.

sleeve_taper_flat_width.$comment: Height above the cuff END mapped to flattened sleeve width. Interpolate linearly between points. Size 6436 only - smaller sizes will be narrower and are the binding case.

garment.note: Only one tunic size measured. A renderer that warns on clearance must either carry a profile per size or state that it is checking against 6436.

breast_pocket_flap_h.note: Corroborated by two other measurements taken independently: the pocket is 15 cm top to bottom and the competition pin strip is 9 cm tall, and 15 - 6 = 9 exactly. The pin band between the flap's lower edge and the pocket's lower seam is therefore precisely the strip, which is what the strip was measured to fill. The previous 4.0 cm placeholder left 11 cm and could not account for the extra 2 cm.

name_tag.note: Standard CAF pattern, laminated and detachable, surname only. BLACK for army and sea cadets, air force blue for air. Obtained locally.

undress_ribbon.note: Worn in rows of at most three with NO interval between ribbons or between rows, so a full row is exactly 10.5 cm wide and each row adds exactly 1.0 cm of height.

national_winner_award.note: The Vamplew & Clement Tremblay Awards (marksmanship) and the Myriam Bedard, Nikki Keddie & Jean-Philippe Le Guellec Awards (biathlon). 'National Winners' in the workbook is SHORTHAND for these, not a separate award. Confirmed by Lt Beal as a NON-STANDARD size: not 1 in square. Poster draws them at aspect 1.07 and about a third larger than the championship pins in the same block. Unmeasured.

medal_court_mount.source_units: 10 cm, top of the medal bar suspender to the bottom edge of the medal
medal_court_mount.note: Court mounting is optional and at no cost to the public, with no minimum number of medals. The ribbons and medals mount on a panel whose size follows the number worn; the panel's lower edge runs in line with the CENTRE of the medals, and each ribbon runs from that lower edge up the front of the panel and back down to the medal. Panel geometry is recorded but not modelled.

air_rank_chevron.source: Hand-measured off issued badges, supplied with the air artwork request. Per key in air badges/air_art_manifest.json (measured_mm).
air_rank_chevron.note: RESOLVED against the poster the same way as the army chevrons. A-CR-CCP-850/DA-003 implies 9.22 / 11.02 / 10.88 / 12.59 cm at 10.5 cm wide: 0.5 to 1.0 cm taller than the ruler, with the biggest excess on the shortest badge. The army poster did exactly the same (0.6 to 1.0 cm, rank_chevron), so it is the art's embroidered field and not a bad measurement, and Corporal's -10.4% needs no re-measure. The measurement governs and the art is stretched to it.

air_rank_lac.source: Lt Beal, 2026-09-24: 8 cm wide, 2 cm at the tallest part.
air_rank_lac.note: Leading Air Cadet, the propeller. The artwork trims to aspect 4.878 against 4.0 measured, 18% flatter than the badge; the measurement governs and the art is stretched to it.

air_rank_warrant.source: Lt Beal, 2026-09-24: use the army MWO and CWO sizes.
air_rank_warrant.note: WO1 inherits the CWO estimate, so the renderer keeps flagging it. The Air WO2 art trims to 1.14:1 in a 1.5:1 box, much as the army MWO poster art (1.26) lost to its measured 3 x 2 in; the WO1 art (0.76) sits within 1% of its box.

air_training_level.note: The poster's 'Proficiency Levels', all five the same size. Poster aspect 1.17 against 1.27 measured; the measurement governs.

air_octagon_badge.source: Hand-measured off issued badges, supplied with the air artwork request. Per key in air badges/air_art_manifest.json (measured_mm).
air_octagon_badge.note: Every Air CTC and proficiency badge is the same octagon. Poster aspect 0.997-1.003 against 1.000 measured, the one Air family where the artwork and the ruler agree. Army's 3.0 cm circle_badge does not apply.

air_squadron_insignia.source: Hand-measured off issued badges, supplied with the air artwork request. Per key in air badges/air_art_manifest.json (measured_mm).
air_squadron_insignia.note: Half-round dome, hung 2 cm below the shoulder seam. Poster aspect 2.253 against 2.076 measured; the measurement governs.

items: Drum Major and Pipe Major appointment insignia
air_unmeasured.note: Drawn in the army 10 x 11 cm appointment box; the Air art is within 1% of that shape. The wings now take the parachutist badge's size and Effective Speaking the championship pins' 1 in square (Lt Beal, 2026-09-24), so this is the last Air size without a decision behind it.

slots.condition: highest level held in each eligible category

conflicts.resolution: 20 cm adopted per CH3S1 3.b.(5). Annex H's 12 cm is geometrically impossible: the marksmanship assembly is anchored at 6 cm and the rifles carry it to roughly 13 cm, so a proficiency badge with its bottom edge at 12 cm would overlap it. Section 1 is the instruction and the annex is illustrative, so Section 1 governs. The resolution rests on that geometry and on Section 1 governing, both of which are checkable. An earlier note claimed corroboration from a photograph of a worn tunic; the photograph was never identified and the claim has been withdrawn rather than left as evidence nobody can produce.

house_rules: Annex H illustrates only two positions. Chapter 3 names three eligible categories (music, first aid, fitness), so the stack is treated as open-ended up to three. LOCAL DECISION.
No precedence order is given in policy for which category sits lowest. Fitness / first aid / music adopted bottom to top. LOCAL DECISION.

Collapse applies within the proficiency stack only. The lowest worn proficiency badge takes the 20 cm slot and the rest chain upward. A missing category does not leave a gap inside the stack. LOCAL DECISION.
notes: The 20 cm anchor is fixed and does not move when marksmanship is absent. A cadet with proficiency badges and no marksmanship wears a visible empty band between 6 cm and 20 cm. This is correct, not a layout error. Renderers must not close the gap.

air.condition: one badge per family, the highest held; the sixth position has no family yet
air.citation: SEWN-3 para 3 Air (e); ANNEX-H 3H-5; Lt Beal, 2026-09-24
air.confirmed: Lt Beal, 2026-09-24: Marksmanship Classification and Glider Pilot Familiarization are worn in this block.

notes: Independent of the proficiency stack. Not a member of it, and does not anchor it. The stack holds at 20 cm whether or not this assembly is present.
Distinguished composition is not illustrated in Annex H. Confirmed locally.

Levels 1-3 are TWO separately sewn pieces: the numeral tab anchored at 6 cm, then 0.5 cm of cloth, then the crossed rifles. Total 7.485 cm tall against 8.0 cm for the single-piece Distinguished. Anchored at the bottom, so the 0.515 cm difference only pushes the top up; nothing sits above before 20 cm, so there is no collision. Both are 6.0 cm wide.

Levels 1-3 are two PHYSICALLY SEPARATE badges, confirmed by Lt Beal handling them: the numeral tab and the crossed rifles are sewn independently with 0.5 cm of cloth between. The sewing guide must therefore emit two rows, not one assembly.
slots.internal_gap_source: CH3S1 3.b.(6) — regulation, not a local measurement

conflicts.source: A-CR-CCP-750/DA-003 artwork, measured off all three levels by recut_marksmanship.py
conflicts.resolution: 0.5 cm stands. It is stated in CH3S1 3.b.(6); the poster is illustrative artwork and carries no dimensions. Same class as Annex H figure 3H-3's 12 cm and its five-badge stagger: where the drawing disagrees with Section 1, Section 1 governs. The range is wide because the poster's rifles are drawn square while the real badge is 6.0 x 5.08 cm, so scaling through height and through width give different answers - further reason not to size from art.

air.note: The upper of Air's two rank anchors per arm. Para 3 says 'centred mid-way' without naming an edge; the figures put the TOP edge on the mid-point (Lt Beal, by inspection). With the elbow still assumed at mid-sleeve (28 cm on 57), the top edge is 14.5 cm below the shoulder seam.

air.condition: rank in [WO2, WO1], with or without an appointment

air.note: Air's senior rank never stacks on an appointment; rank_senior_no_appointment covers WO2 and WO1 either way.

notes: Annex H illustrates only the band appointment. CH3S1 3.b.(8) is generic to any appointment insignia.

'Chevron points' means the lowest points of the badge, so the badge builds UPWARD from 20 cm. Confirmed by Annex H 3H-4-3, which draws the drum major badge clearly above the CTC grid, not overlapping it.

Terminology inconsistency in Annex H: the Sgt rule says chevron 'tips' 1 cm below the RCAC badge (apex, i.e. top edge), the appointment rule says chevron 'points' at 20 cm (leg ends, i.e. bottom edge). Same word family, opposite edge. Do not generalise one to the other.
Eligible appointment insignia list not yet sourced. See Annex E.

Drum Major and Pipe Major are the only appointments carrying insignia. Established from the poster's APPOINTMENT section and confirmed by Lt Beal; Annex E was never sourced and is no longer being waited on.

air.rule: Takes whichever right-sleeve rank anchor the rank leaves free: the LOWER (bottom 9 cm above the cuff top) for Cadet and LAC to FSgt, the UPPER (top edge on the elbow-shoulder mid-point) for WO2 and WO1.
air.citation: SEWN-3 para 3 Air (f); ANNEX-H 3H-5 / 3H-6; Lt Beal, 2026-09-24
air.note: A dedicated spot, unlike Army, which pushes the senior rank up off the appointment. A Cadet holding an appointment has both anchors free; the lower is used, as for every non-WO rank.
air.confirmed: Lt Beal, 2026-09-24. A Cadet holding an appointment probably never happens, but isn't known to be impossible; the lower anchor is used.

slots.supersession: advanced qualification supersedes basic within the same qualification stream
slots.condition: CTC qualification, staff, deployment or exchange insignia held

conflicts.alternate_value: three bottom with two directly on top, bottom edges touching
conflicts.resolution: Aligned 2x3 grid adopted per CH3S1 3.b.(9) and the drawn figures. The Annex H text version describes only five positions and omits the centre-out fill order.

Right arm adopted per ANNEX-H Figure 3H-6, which Lt Beal treats as authoritative: para 3 is a typo here. As written, (g) puts the CTC block on the left arm 'immediately above the top of the cuff', exactly where (e) puts the proficiency block, so the instruction cannot be followed. This is the one recorded case where a figure beats the instruction, and only because the instruction contradicts itself. Its 'second insignia to the left of the first, to the front of the sleeve' points both ways on the right arm; 'front' is kept, as on Army's right-arm grid.
Order awarded adopted per CH3S1 3.b.(9). Lt Beal: the section text is dated newer than the Annex D figure notes, so it governs where they differ.

conflicts.alternate_value: 7, the seventh placed immediately over the fourth
conflicts.resolution: Six adopted per SEWN-3 para 3 (g), the newer text (Lt Beal). This is where the old seventh-badge note came from. The same 3D-5 note puts the block on the RIGHT sleeve, corroborating Figure 3H-6 against para 3's left.

notes: 'front' is toward the chest, 'rear' is toward the back. On the right sleeve viewed flat from outside, front is image-right. Output sewing guides in front/rear terms, not left/right, or the block will be mirrored.

air.citation: ANNEX-H 3H-6 and CH3-ANNEX-D 3D-5 for the arm; SEWN-3 para 3 Air (g) for the rest
air.note: Right arm per both figures; para 3 says left (see conflicts). Staff and exchange insignia share the block; Effective Speaking does not. Para 3 also lists Deployment insignia, but Air has none currently (Lt Beal, 2026-09-24). Supersession is not stated for Air.

slots.supersession_status: Stated for Army in CH3S1 3.b.(9) and the Figure 3D-3 note. How it applies is unclear for every element (Lt Beal, 2026-09-24), so the renderer does not apply it: every badge selected is drawn. See open questions.

slots.condition: highest star level held that carries a badge
house_rules: ALP has no star insignia of its own yet, so an ALP cadet continues to wear the Gold Star - the highest level they hold that carries a badge. This follows from the general rule below rather than being a special case, so the slot is never vacant and no phantom box is needed. Confirmed by Lt Beal. SUPERSEDES the earlier LOCAL DECISION that left the slot empty and held the CTC grid's position.

air.condition: highest training level held; not worn by WO2 or WO1
air.note: Air's own name for them, on the poster and per Lt Beal, and what the rail and the drawing say. Para 3 calls them training level insignia. Not the cuff proficiency badges, which are a different thing with a confusingly similar name. All five levels carry a badge.
air.name: Proficiency Level 1-5

slots.fill: rows fill from the bottom; a partial row goes on TOP, centred on the row below
slots.order: precedence 1 is highest and sits on the TOP row, closest to the centre of the chest; numbering runs outward and downward from there
notes: No interval between ribbons within a row, and none between rows. A row of three is exactly 10.5 cm wide; each extra row adds exactly 1.0 cm.
On the RIGHT breast viewed from the front, the centre of the chest is image-right, so precedence 1 sits at the inboard end of the top row.
A full row of three is 10.5 cm at the locally measured 3.5 x 1.0 cm ribbon, against a 13 cm pocket - fits with 1.25 cm each side.
Precedence order is NOT in Chapter 5. It is in CATO 13-16, unsourced.

air.source: Lt Beal, 2026-09-24: placed the same on an Air tunic as on an Army one.

notes: One row if they fit. From five medals the renderer overlaps them horizontally, highest priority fully visible. Five is a drawing choice, not a rule: the real limit is the wearer's arm seam (next note).
Maximum mounting width is set by the wearer's physique, not a number: centred on the pocket, the bar must not run past the jacket arm seam. The renderer flags this rather than computing it.
Length is 10 cm, suspender top to medal bottom edge (CH5-S7), so the medal finishes 9 cm down a 15 cm pocket.

Precedence order is not in Chapter 5. CATO 13-16 para 19, the cadet-programme authority, gives it for ten medals, and they are CJCRGPO-10050 7.4's eleven in the same order less the Order of St. George, which CATO leaves out and which rests on 10050 alone.

PRECEDENCE (CJCRGPO-10050 7.4): the full CJCR list is 11 medals. Seven are available to an army cadet - seq 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8 and 10 - and the other four are Sea or Air awards. Keep the full list and sort by seq rather than storing the army seven, because a cadet who transferred in from another element retains an award earned there and it must slot into the right position.
Precedence 1 is worn INBOARD, nearest the centre of the chest, consistent with right_ribbons. 7.4 says only 'side by side'; the inboard-first convention comes from CH5-A 5A-1.

Precedence was first adopted from CJCRGPO-10050 7.4 on Lt Beal's direction, before CATO 13-16 was obtained: the CJCR honours committee sets precedence for both programmes (10050 4.2) and the 7.4 list spans all three elements. CATO 13-16 para 19 has since confirmed it for every medal but St. George.

Artwork: ribbons 35 x 10 mm; medals 46 x 100 mm, a 35 mm ribbon centred on a canvas sized off the widest claw-bar return. Authored as SVG, not extracted from the poster, which never carried the medals. Every face is traced from supplied artwork except the fouled anchor on the two navy medals; suspensions, bars and sprigs are drawn. Fidelity per key in Medals and Ribbons/medal_art_manifest.json.

Overhang: on a real group the suspension bars, claws and connectors overhang the ribbon onto the neighbouring medal (Lt Beal, 2026-09-24). The renderer keeps the pitch at the ribbon width and draws each medal's art at its own canvas width, centred on its slot, senior on top; every box and check stays the ribbon. The full medal delivery of 2026-09-24 first made room by shrinking the ribbon to 80% of a 35 mm canvas, which opened a 7 mm gap between ribbons; it was resized the same day to a 35 mm ribbon on a 46 mm canvas and merged.

order_of_precedence.medal: Royal Canadian Legion Cadet Medal of Excellence
Navy League of Canada Medal of Excellence

order_of_precedence.note: Replaces the Major-General W.A. Howard Award at CATO 13-16 para 19.e (Army Cadet League of Canada). Four award bars, junior to senior: Rodger, Howard, President, Walsh. The medal is never worn bare - at least one bar - and Walsh requires President, giving 11 wearable states. Both rules confirmed by Lt Beal.

Drawn since 0.25. No text source describes the ribbon: Blatherwick gives the terms of the award and stops. A-CR-CCP-850/DA-003 shows the medal in full colour: seven stripes, navy, light blue and maroon, sampled off that image with the width assumed at the standard 35 mm. 0.29 and 0.30 recorded Lt Beal's first read, that it looks like the ANAVETS palette, and assumed the poster's print had shifted the colours as it did the Air Cadet Service Medal's gold. It hadn't: a reference photo in Lt Beal's corrections to the artwork creator shows navy, light blue and maroon, and Lt Beal adopted it (Lt Beal, 2026-09-24). The medal pack draws it that way: widths 9/9/9/46/9/9/9 and colours both read off that photo, fidelity MEASURED pattern / MEASURED colour. The 46% centre replaces 41% taken from the poster.

items: Medal and suspender dimensions (Chapter 5 gives placement but no sizes).
Breast pocket flap height, which every pocket-mounted pin depends on.
Shirt layouts. Only the jacket is modelled; the DofE pin is jacket-only and the poppy figure is drawn for the shirt.

Canadian Honours System medals (Queen's Jubilee and similar). A cadet may hold one, but the CO must seek wear instructions through the chain of command. Chapter 5 covers only National Cadet Honours and Awards. One data point: CJCRGPO-10050 7.3 wears a Canadian Order, decoration or medal on the LEFT side of the chest, opposite the cadet awards - consistent with national practice, but stated for the JCR sweatshirt, so it is a hint and not an instruction for the tunic.

global_limits.rule: Proficiency: only the highest level achieved in each category is worn.
Marksmanship: only the highest achievement is worn.
Star level: the highest level held that CARRIES A BADGE is worn. ALP has no badge, so an ALP cadet wears Gold.
Appointment: only one appointment insignia is worn.
CTC / staff / deployment / exchange: maximum six combined.
Participation / competition pins: maximum three combined. Not yet modelled, front of tunic.
Commemorative pins: maximum one. Not yet modelled, front of tunic.
Badges are sewn with thread matched to the base cloth. Never glued or ironed.

General: within any category where only the highest is worn, 'highest' means the highest level that carries a badge. A level marked not_worn in QualMap (ALP, Fitness 'Participated') is skipped and the next one down is worn.
global_limits.citation: CH3S1 3.b.(5), 3.b.(6), 3.b.(10); resolves the ALP case without a special rule

global_limits.rule: Undress ribbons: maximum three per row, no interval between ribbons or rows. A fourth ribbon starts a new row, centred on the row below.
Medals and undress ribbons are alternatives - undress ribbons represent the medals when the medals themselves are not worn. Never both.
Commendation and DofE pins: multiple pins are worn one above the other, 0.5 cm apart, in precedence order CDS > Command > Cadet > Navy League > DofE.
The Duke of Edinburgh pin is worn on the JACKET ONLY. Cadet commendation pins may be worn on either the jacket or the shirt.

Every undress ribbon is drawn 3.5 cm wide, including the four whose issued width differs: Bravery 3.8 cm per CATO 13-16 Annex B (3.6 cm per Blatherwick, contested), Lord Strathcona 3.2 cm, Navy League Medal of Excellence 3.8 cm, Sea Cadet Service Medal 3.8 cm. LOCAL DECISION, Lt Beal: rows are laid three across with no interval, so one odd width breaks the row. True widths are recorded in the artwork manifest.
global_limits.citation: LOCAL DECISION; true widths per CATO 13-16 Annex B and Blatherwick

open_questions: CWO rank dimensions still an estimate, though poster aspect 0.753 matches the 0.750 guess.
Only tunic size 6436 measured. Clearance warnings need a profile per size, or a stated assumption.
Annex H figure 3H-3 carries an incorrect dimension. Worth reporting up so it gets corrected at the national level.

Corps name title dimensions (12.21 x 3.85 cm) are DERIVED from the poster's title-plus-badge template and the measured 6.35 cm badge diameter, not measured directly. Worth checking a real title with a ruler.
Annex B lists national and cadet commendations in one 0.5 cm stack while Annex D puts them on opposite pockets. Resolved in favour of Annex D as the more specific source - confirm with RCSU.
National-winner award pins (Vamplew / Clement Tremblay, and Bedard / Keddie / Le Guellec) are confirmed non-standard in size and have never been measured. Drawn at 1 in.

Figure 5D-1 puts National Commendations on the LEFT pocket; the renderer still draws one right-hand stack. CJCRGPO-10050 7.5 now corroborates 5D-1 (CDS and VCDS marked 'to be worn on the left side'). Two sources against one reading. DECISION NEEDED: flip the renderer to a split stack.
Medal bar maximum width is physique-dependent (must not pass the jacket arm seam). Needs a per-cadet measurement or it stays a flag.

Duke of Edinburgh pin: the ASPECT is known - the issued artwork for all three levels is 1.197 - so only the absolute size is a guess. Drawn 2.0 cm wide, which makes it 2.0 x 1.671. Annex D still gives no millimetres. Note it is issued at three levels, so it cannot be represented by a single pin.
NRT and Bisley Series pin sizes (RCAC National Rifle Team, LGen C.H. Belzile Trophy) are unmeasured and non-standard - artwork trims to aspect 2.47 and 1.42, so neither is a 1 in square.
Order of St George is on the poster but absent from D - Qual Info, which carries only six medals. Add it as a seventh.

RESOLVED: the medals were never extractable from the poster, which carries them as photographs. They are authored as SVG in Medals and Ribbons/ instead, and since 0.32 every face is traced from supplied artwork. Was: Medal artwork: all seven medals are still unextracted. They are photographs, so extract_badges.py never saw them - same failure as the fitness block and the pins.
Commendation and award insignia artwork (CDS, Command, Cadet, Navy League) is illustrated in Annex D but not extracted; the renderer draws plain bars at the right size.
Sashes and lanyards are not modelled and no source has been identified for them.
A full-tunic render is not attempted. The tool draws four flat panels, and the shoulder-to-pocket relationship is presentational rather than measured.

Sea and Air elements are out of scope. The coordinate model and resolver should carry over unchanged; the rules pack, the artwork and the nametag colour are element-specific (air cadet name tags are air force blue).
CJCRGPO-10050 contradicts itself on the second-tier commendation: 5.1 offers a 'Comd CJCR Commendation', 7.5 ranks a 'VCDS Commendation'. Same slot under two names, or two awards?

If national commendations move to the left pocket, the left pocket needs its own stack geometry. 5D-1 gives the single-pin case (centred between the lower seam and the flap's lower edge) but not the two-pin case, and CDS + VCDS is possible.

A cadet transferring between elements retains awards earned there (the principle is stated for JCR at CJCRGPO-10050 6.2). Confirm it holds for cadets, since it is what makes the Sea and Air entries in the 11-medal list reachable on an army tunic.

Cadet Service Medal bars: the ARMY scheme is now sourced. ACLC Policy 13.1 paras 5 and 12 - four years earns the medal, each further year adds a gold bar on the medal and a gold maple leaf on the undress ribbon, accumulating rather than replacing. The tool offers 4/5/6/7 years. Maximum: Blatherwick ch 40 says a cadet enrolling on their 12th birthday and leaving the day before their 19th could receive a third bar, so three bars (seven years) is the ceiling by arithmetic and the tool's 7 is no longer a local decision; Policy 13.1 itself sets no limit (artwork creator's NOTES.md). Still open: the SEA and AIR service medals use different schemes - Sea reportedly uses anchor devices rather than an accumulating stack, Air's bars exist commercially but no source describes them. Sea is drawn base state only. AIR, per Lt Beal, 2026-09-24: the same accumulating system as Army, with its own devices: each further year adds a gold bar with a bird, wings spread, on the medal, and a rosette rather than a maple leaf on the undress ribbon. Drawn since 0.32 from the 2026-09-24 medal pack: the bar's eagle and the ribbon rosette are stylised, the disc's RCAirC emblem traced from League artwork.

The Sea, Army and Air Cadet Service Medals are modelled as one award in three elements, exclusive by the element the cadet served in, with a transfer carrying the earlier one. Confirm a cadet cannot hold two.

Order of St. George is absent from CATO 13-16 para 19 entirely. Its seq 8 position rests on CJCR Gp O 10050 para 7.4 alone, which is a JCR order. Every other medal in the list is now confirmed against CATO; this one is not, and a cadet holding it could be wearing it in the wrong place in the group.

RESOLVED in 0.25. Air Force Association Medal (CATO 13-16 para 19.f): no text source describes its ribbon, but A-CR-CCP-850/DA-003 shows it in full colour. The medal pack now carries medal_afa / ribbon_afa, colour sampled off that image and geometry estimated at the standard 35 mm, and seq 6 is drawn. It is an air-element award and reaches an army tunic only by transfer. 0.29 recorded the ANAVETS palette on Lt Beal's first read; 0.31 reverts it to navy, light blue and maroon on a reference photo (Lt Beal), which is what the poster shows. See right_medals, seq 6.

PARTLY RESOLVED in 0.32. Faces: every medal face is traced from supplied artwork except the fouled anchor on the Navy League and Sea Cadet Service medals, which is drawn, as are the suspensions, bars and the AFA's laurel sprigs. Ribbons: Bravery and ANAVETS remain ESTIMATED, their stripe order sourced (CATO 13-16 Annex B and Blatherwick ch 40) but widths and hues by eye; Navy League, Sea and Air Service have measured widths and estimated colours. Per key in the artwork manifest. Was: Medal and ribbon artwork fidelity is mixed and recorded per item in the artwork manifest. Lord Strathcona, RCL Excellence, Order of St. George and the Army Cadet Service Medal are sampled from source images; Bravery and ANAVETS stripe widths are still eyeballed; every medallion obverse is stylised because the central relief is not reproducible from the sources to hand.

RESOLVED by Sewn Insignia para 3. Sea does not stack three things above the left cuff: proficiency insignia (up to six) go on the LOWER RIGHT sleeve, and the left arm above the cuff carries up to four Staff / Deployment / Exchange / appointment insignia combined, of which only one may be an appointment. The renderer now draws zero clashes for Sea.

Sea and Air geometry is SOURCED from Sewn Insignia para 3, with one assumption left: the elbow. 'Mid-way between the elbow and the shoulder seam' needs an elbow position, taken as mid-sleeve, 28 cm on a 57 cm sleeve, giving 42.5 cm. Measure a real sleeve to settle it. Air uses the army tunic's measurements (Lt Beal), so its '9 cm above the top of the cuff' is y = 14 on the 5 cm cuff. AIR RESOLVED in 0.26: which edge sits mid-way. Figures 3H-5 / 3H-6 put the TOP edge on the mid-point (Lt Beal). The bottom-edge reading drawn in 0.25 ran every chevron rank into the squadron insignia; top-edge clears it by 7.3 cm. Sea's edge is still unknown and still drawn bottom-edge.

Sea artwork does not exist: Sea draws ARMY artwork for rank, training level and proficiency badges, so a sea Petty Officer renders as an army chevron. Correct structure, wrong picture. Air is RESOLVED in 0.25: air_art_pack.js (63 badges from A-CR-CCP-850/DA-003) is wired in, and shared rows find their Air picture by the air_ prefix.
Sea's corps title slot is modelled (a rectangular title directly below the shoulder title, which is common to all sea cadets) but has no dimensions and no artwork.

RESOLVED in 0.26, superseded. This note predates para 3. Air's CTC block starts immediately above the top of the cuff on the RIGHT arm (Figure 3H-6), six maximum, and the training level sits on the left arm with its bottom 9 cm above the cuff (para 3 (d)). The seven-badge rule was wrong; see 33.

RESOLVED in 0.26: Air pilot wings are modelled (slot front_left_pilot_wings), sourced to para 3 (a) and CH3 Annex D Figure 3D-6. 3D-6 also supplies the rule that the Glider Pilot CTC badge is never worn with Glider Pilot Wings, which the renderer raises as a crit. Power supersedes Glider, and a single dropdown enforces highest only. Para 3's 0.5 cm against 3D-6's 'directly above' is recorded as a conflict on the slot.

Element-specific participation insignia: Sea's Regatta series is still not modelled, and Sea shows the army Bisley stream in its place. Sea wears Staff Cadet on the lower LEFT sleeve and everything else lower right. RESOLVED for Air in 0.26: Effective Speaking is a competition pin series, not a sewn badge. It takes the top-of-precedence place in the left-pocket pin strip that Army gives the Bisley Series (Lt Beal), and para 3 (g)'s CTC block (CTC, Staff, Deployment, Exchanges) never included it. The first Effective Speaking artwork arrived fully opaque with white corners; the re-cut (air pack revision 2) keys the white paper out, and nothing else in the pack changed. Confirmed by Lt Beal: worn with the championship pins, above them, inside the three-pin limit.

RESOLVED in 0.26: the Air CTC block is on the RIGHT arm per Figure 3H-6. Para 3 put both the six proficiency insignia and the six CTC / Staff / Deployment / Exchange insignia on the LEFT arm, both immediately above the cuff, which cannot be done; Lt Beal confirms a typo. Recorded as a conflict on ctc_grid.

RESOLVED in 0.26: Air has four rank anchors, upper and lower on each arm (Figures 3H-5 / 3H-6). LAC to FSgt use the upper pair, WO2 and WO1 the lower, and an appointment takes whichever right-sleeve anchor the rank leaves free (Lt Beal). Para 3 (f) attaches both positions to WO2 and WO1. The reading 0.22 adopted (9 cm for WO2/WO1, mid-way for the rest) put the appointment on top of the rank every time, and the renderer had in fact been drawing every Air appointment at the cuff.

RESOLVED in 0.26: six. Para 3 says six for each block, twice, and Figures 3H-5 / 3H-6 agree. The earlier seven-badge note was wrong. Found in 0.29: the seven-badge rule is the CH3 Annex D Figure 3D-5 note, which Lt Beal dates older than para 3. Recorded as a conflict on ctc_grid; six stands.

Sea's corps badge is worn on the RIGHT BREAST, centred 3 cm above the pocket, moving to 4.5 cm with a second row of ribbons and 5.5 cm with a third. Not drawn yet, and it interacts with the ribbon rows the tool already lays out, so it should be straightforward to add.

RESOLVED in 0.26, see 29. Air's Glider / Power Pilot sewn wings are drawn centred 0.5 cm above the LEFT breast pocket, highest level only, with the Glider CTC exclusion raised as a crit. Artwork is in the air pack; size unmeasured.

Sea's proficiency arrangement is unspecified. Para 3 gives the sleeve, the anchor and the maximum of six but not the layout, so the renderer chains them vertically the way the army stack does. Air's is RESOLVED in 0.26: para 3 (e)'s 1-2-3 / 4-5-6 fill is applied from the top of the cuff in award order, with the order the dropdowns were set standing in until dates exist.

RESOLVED in 0.26: Air Marksmanship Classification (Marksman, First Class, Expert, Distinguished) is drawn in the six-badge cuff block through the marksmanship dropdown, as air_mk_1 to air_mk_4, one piece each. Found in the air poster inventory; worn as a proficiency badge per para 3 (e) and Lt Beal.

Air's families are Physical Fitness, First Aid, Music, Marksmanship Classification and Glider Pilot Familiarization; the sixth position has no family yet. AIR: the poster calls the training level badges 'Proficiency Levels', which is the tool's word for the six cuff insignia. Same word, different badges. Kept as training_level here.

RESOLVED in 0.25: medal_afa / ribbon_afa are in the medal pack and seq 6 is drawn. AIR: the Air Force Association Medal appears in full colour on the air poster, which settles the question that had it omitted from the tool as unsourced. Slot 6 can be unhidden once medal_afa / ribbon_afa are added to the medal pack.

RESOLVED in 0.29: GOLD. The Air Cadet Service Medal disc is gold (Lt Beal, 2026-09-24), as Blatherwick says. The air poster prints it brown (sampled mean #9E7B60, hue 26 degrees against gold's 44) and it was built bronze in 0.25 off that; reverted, with the gold artwork restored and medal_specs.py back to gold. The poster's colour is not reliable for metal. The same image does confirm the Blatherwick ribbon description.

AIR: the squadron shoulder insignia is a half-round dome with the element name arched over the top, squadron number large in the centre and squadron name below - a different shape from Army's scrolled corps title, and it needs two text fields rather than one. The existing corps-title generator cannot produce it. In 0.25 the two poster samples draw as the Air unit choices (89 Pacific, 96 Alouette), sized from the 4.25 in x 52 mm measurement.

CTC supersession is unclear for every element (Lt Beal, 2026-09-24). CH3S1 3.b.(9) and the Figure 3D-3 note say 'advanced qualification supersedes basic qualification' for Army; Air's texts (Figure 3D-5, para 3 (g)) and Sea's don't. Which badges count as advanced and basic, and whether it applies outside Army, is open. The renderer does not apply it: every badge selected is drawn.

Precedence between the commendation pins and the competition pins is unclear for every element (Lt Beal, 2026-09-24). Air follows Army for now: commendation pins in one right-pocket stack, competition pins in the left-pocket strip.

AIR proficiency block: when a cadet moves up within a family (Music Basic to Level 1, Bronze to Silver), does the new badge keep the old one's position or take the next free one? The renderer keeps the position. The block also holds six against five known families; the sixth is unknown.
CTC cap: once more badges are held than may be worn (six), which come off? The renderer drops the most recently awarded. Unsourced for every element.

Medal mounting, swing or court. Every medal is drawn swing-mounted, its ribbon ending at the suspender, at the 10 cm court-mount length (measured_constants_cm.medal_court_mount), and the front note calls that 'Court mounted'. The 10 cm comes from CH5-S7, the court-mounting section, so whether a swing-mounted medal hangs to the same length is unsourced. Court-mount artwork, with the ribbon carried down behind the disc to the medal centre line, doesn't exist yet: make_medals.py's court option only adds a pin bar, and its PANEL_BOTTOM constant is unused. A request for medal_<key>_court twins on the same 35 x 100 mm canvas is written; the renderer will offer swing or court once they exist.

changelog.change: RCAC sleeve badge measured at 2.5 in (6.35 cm) diameter; corps name title derived from it at 12.21 x 3.85 cm using the poster's shared template.
ALP cadets wear the Gold Star, not a vacant slot. Generalised to: wear the highest level in a category that carries a badge. Removes the phantom-box local decision.

Competition and expedition pin artwork recovered from the poster. Championship pins confirmed 1 in square; national-winner awards recorded as non-standard and unmeasured. 'National Winners' documented as workbook shorthand.

Expedition insignia corrected to the RIGHT pocket, 0.5 cm above the nametag, per the CH5-B figure; it had wrongly been carried as a left-pocket pin stream as well. Conflict with the workbook's out_of_scope_left_pocket recorded. National Rifle Team placement marked unvalidated.

Nametag sits flush on the pocket top when nothing is suspended. Medals hang from the ribbon line and spill over the pocket, so the nametag does not move for them. Left-pocket pin precedence sourced (Bisley, then CCM Marksmanship, then CCM Biathlon), which also confirms the Bisley pins belong on that pocket. Vacant Master Cadet / NSE slot no longer drawn.
Medal length fixed at 10 cm by the court mounting rule, replacing a guessed hang. Court mounting panel geometry recorded.

Aligned the front with the Chapter 5 review: order of dress gates medals (C1) against undress ribbons (C2/C3/C3B); all five commendation pins moved into one right-pocket stack with the real Annex D sizes; stack repositions under the medals when worn; medals overlap past four; slots renamed to right_medals / right_ribbons / right_commendation_stack. CATO 13-16 recorded as blocking.
Shoulder title artwork swapped from the poster's Lord Westminster 2990 example to 242 Fredericton, title case. Same plate, same geometry.

Open questions extended with Lt Beal's review: NRT/Bisley pin sizes, the seventh medal (Order of St George) missing from QualMap, medal and commendation artwork, sashes and lanyards, a full-tunic render, and Sea/Air.

Added CJCR Gp O 10050 (JCR National Honours and Awards) as a secondary source. Medals now carry an 11-entry order of precedence from 7.4, seven of which an army cadet can hold. 7.5 corroborates Figure 5D-1's national-left / cadet-right commendation split, moving the right_commendation_stack conflict from unresolved to decision-needed. Recorded 10050's own internal contradiction between the Comd CJCR Commendation (5.1) and the VCDS Commendation (7.5).

Breast pocket flap height measured at 6.0 cm (Lt Beal), replacing the 4.0 cm placeholder. This moves every pocket-mounted pin. It also closes a gap: the pin band is now exactly the 9 cm of the measured competition pin strip, since the pocket is 15 cm and 15 - 6 = 9. Open question closed.

Service medal modelled as one award in three elements plus a bar selection, rather than three separate medals; precedence still comes from seq 9/10/11. Bars are recorded and named but not drawn, and the whole bar scheme is logged as unsourced.

Three questions closed on Lt Beal's authority. Chevron heights and the MWO aspect resolve to the hand measurements against the poster art, with the reasoning recorded on the constants rather than left open. Chapter 7 of the Dress Instructions is confirmed as the JCR chapter, so it does not supersede the Chapter 5 citations. Also: the Protected A workbook has been moved out of this directory.

Four questions closed on Lt Beal's direction. Medal and ribbon precedence adopted from 10050 7.4 without waiting on CATO 13-16. Appointment insignia confirmed as Drum Major and Pipe Major without waiting on Annex E. The fitness crops, Excellence included, confirmed correct. The claim that the 20 cm proficiency anchor was corroborated by a photograph is withdrawn: the photograph could not be identified, and the geometric argument stands without it.

Medal, ribbon and commendation-pin artwork wired in; every award now draws as itself rather than a plain bar. CATO 13-16 para 19 sourced verbatim, confirming the precedence for all but the Order of St. George. Seq 5 is the Army Cadet Medal of Merit with four award bars and two wearability rules; seq 6, the Air Force Association Medal, is omitted as unsourced. Uniform 3.5 cm ribbon width recorded as a local decision. DofE sized from the artwork's own aspect.

Sleeve slot ids renamed from positional to semantic (left_marksmanship -> marksmanship, right_rank_junior -> rank_junior) and the two duplicated pairs merged (corps_name, element_badge). Which arm a slot is worn on now belongs to the element rather than to the slot's name, which is the prerequisite for Sea (rank left) and Air (rank both arms). Army geometry is unchanged and the rendered output was verified byte-identical.

Sea and Air populated with the structure Lt Beal supplied: rank names and the junior/senior split, training levels (same system as the army star, different terminology and artwork, and a level 5 badge both elements carry), sea appointments and proficiencies, element-specific summer training, and participation insignia. Summer training rows are now tagged tri-service or army-only. star_level renamed training_level since it is not army-specific. Slot PRESENCE is per element: neither Sea nor Air wears an RCAC badge or a marksmanship badge, and Sea splits the shoulder title into a common title plus a corps title. All Sea and Air geometry is guessed and flagged; army output verified byte-identical.

Sea and Air placement sourced from Sewn Insignia para 3, replacing the guesses. Sea: rank left arm at two heights, CTC upper right (max 2), proficiency lower right (max 6), and a combined max-four Staff/Deployment/Exchange/appointment group on the left arm above the cuff - which resolves the three-way collision previously flagged. Air: squadron insignia 2 cm below the seam, rank both arms with WO2/WO1 low, training level left arm and NOT worn by WO2/WO1, appointment on the right sleeve. Two contradictions inside the air text logged and drawn as written. Army output verified byte-identical.

Air poster inventory folded in. Removed air_power: the Power Pilot Scholarship yields wings only and has no CTC badge, confirmed by the dress instruction and by its absence from the poster. Added air_oshkosh and air_exchange, and dropped the duplicate air_staff, since Staff Cadet is a tri-service row. Summer training is 24 badges for Air, 13 of them tri-service courses that share a row with Army but not a badge - handled by an element-prefixed art key. Six findings from the inventory logged, including that Air wears marksmanship after all.

Air artwork keys settled on one rule, air_ + the key the tool already uses for that badge's row, so shared rows resolve by prefix with no mapping table: proficiency is air_fit_* / air_fa_* / air_mus_* / air_mk_*, appointments air_appt_drum_major / air_appt_pipe_major. Corrected open question 38, which said Air Music is six badges against Army's five; both are six. Recorded Air marksmanship as one piece per badge. Flagged Effective Speaking as pins on the air poster, against the note that puts it in the sewn CTC block. The eight championship pins on the air poster are the army pack's own (seven byte-identical images, the eighth the same photograph cropped tighter), so none are requested.

Air artwork wired in. air_art_pack.js (63 badges, A-CR-CCP-850/DA-003) merges into the page like the medals: ranks, training levels and the squadron insignia carry air_ keys, and shared rows (CTC, fitness, first aid, music, appointments) find Air art through one element-prefix lookup. Air sizes come from hand measurements where they exist - chevrons 10.5 cm wide at 8.255 / 10.16 / 10.16 / 12.065 cm, training level 3.81 x 3.0, every octagon 3.066, squadron insignia 10.795 x 5.2 - with LAC's height and both Warrant Officers estimated from the artwork. Fixed the Flight Sergeant drawing at 14 cm with the Warrant Officers: it was missing from the mid-way list. Medal pack updated: the Air Force Association Medal is drawn at seq 6 and the Air Cadet Service Medal disc is bronze. Army and Sea output verified unchanged.

Air placement settled from Figures 3H-5 / 3H-6, CH3 Annex D 3D-6 and Lt Beal's answers, and written into per-slot elements.air blocks. CTC block moved to the right arm (conflict recorded: para 3 says left, a typo). Four rank anchors: LAC to FSgt with the top edge on the elbow-shoulder mid-point, WO2 and WO1 with the bottom 9 cm above the cuff, and the appointment takes whichever right-sleeve anchor is free. Proficiency is the 2x3 block from the cuff in award order, one badge per family, adding marksmanship, glider familiarization and Music Basic. Pilot wings modelled on the left breast with the 3D-6 Glider exclusion (conflict recorded: 0.5 cm against 'directly above'). Effective Speaking tops the Air pin strip. LAC measured 8 x 2 cm; Air adopts the army tunic's measurements. Fixed an unsized marksmanship box drawn for any element without the slot. Army output unchanged; Sea loses only an army-only RCAC note.

Sizes for the last unmeasured Air badges, per Lt Beal: WO2 and WO1 take the army MWO (7.62 x 5.08, measured) and CWO (7.62 x 10.16, still an estimate) sizes, the pilot wings the army parachutist badge's 9.0 x 3.87, and the Effective Speaking pins the championship pins' 1 in square. Only the Air appointments are left on an adopted army size with no decision recorded.

Air follow-up delivery merged: Effective Speaking pins re-cut with the white paper keyed out (the other 60 air badges byte-identical), and the medal sources that match the medal pack (medal_specs.py with afa at seq 6, the bronze Air service disc and an empty UNSOURCED; the manifest regenerates from it identically). Air's training level badges are named Proficiency Level 1-5 in the rail and the drawing, per Lt Beal.

Lt Beal's answers to the Air officer questions. Front layout confirmed the same as Army (confirmed_shared on the front slots). Appointment reading, the cuff-block families and the Effective Speaking pin placement confirmed. Pilot wings moved onto the pocket edge: 3D-6 separates the sewn wings from the shirt pin, and para 3's 0.5 cm is the pin's gap. Figures 3D-3 and 3D-5 added; two conflicts recorded where they disagree with the newer section text (Army sequence basis, Air maximum of seven), and 3D-5 corroborates the Air CTC block on the right arm. Air Cadet Service Medal disc is gold, reverting 0.25's bronze. Air service bars described (bird bar, rosettes). New open questions: supersession, commendation versus competition pin precedence, Air level-ups within a family, and which CTC badges come off past the cap.

Cleanup before publishing. right_medals: the overlap note said 'past about five' against the renderer's five or more; corrected, and marked as a drawing choice rather than a rule. Seq 6, the Air Force Association Medal, still carried 'available: false' and 'NOT RENDERED' from before 0.25; brought up to date, and Lt Beal's ANAVETS palette recorded, which had lived only in the artwork follow-up. New open question: medals are drawn swing-mounted at the court-mount length and labelled court mounted, and court-mount artwork doesn't exist yet.

Medal artwork review (full delivery, 2026-09-24). Overhang modelled: bars and connectors overhang the neighbouring medal (Lt Beal), so the renderer draws a medal's art at its own canvas width, centred on its 3.5 cm slot; the delivery's 80% ribbon goes back for a wider canvas instead. AFA ribbon reverts to navy / light blue / maroon on a reference photo (Lt Beal), undoing 0.29-0.30's ANAVETS palette. Service bar ceiling sourced: Blatherwick ch 40 gives three bars by arithmetic. CATO 13-16 para 19 now cited as the precedence authority in right_medals and in the renderer's messages, which still called it unsourced.

Resized medal pack merged: 35 mm ribbons on a 46 mm canvas, drawn centred on the 3.5 cm pitch so the metal overhangs the neighbouring medal. Every face now traced, the Air service bars drawn, the AFA provenance corrected by the creator. Resolver output unchanged across the harness scenarios.

orders_of_dress.$comment: Chapter 5 renders differently by order of dress. Nothing on the sleeves depends on this; the right breast does.
orders_of_dress.outerwear: None of Chapter 5 is worn on outerwear.

$slot_ids: Sleeve slot ids are SEMANTIC, not positional. Which arm a slot lands on is set per element in the tool's ELEMENTS table, because that is what differs: Army wears rank on the right arm, Sea on the left, Air on both. A slot named right_rank could not express that. Breast slots keep their side, which is anatomical rather than element-varying.
